svg.title: The four regulated tables, what each one proves, and what links them
svg.desc: The four tables the lead pipeline owns, drawn apart from the content tables because they are governed differently. Drizzle owns all four; Payload owns the content tables beside them in the same database, and neither migrator may touch the other's. Leads carry the TCPA consent evidence: the exact disclosure text shown, its version, and the moment of agreement, because a boolean is not evidence. Scope of Appointment records carry a signature, a signing time, the product types agreed to and the attestation text with its version. Do-not-contact requests carry an email and a phone reduced to its last ten digits, which is the canonical form the suppression lookup uses; they are indexed on both. The outbox references a lead and is deleted with it, and its idempotency key is unique so a retry cannot create a second contact in the CRM. Three of the four carry a hashed address salted with the application secret, which is why rotating that secret severs every hash at once. Leads and Scope of Appointment records carry a retention date ten years out; suppression rows carry none, because a suppression has to outlive the record it suppresses.
